The Requirements for Getting a UAE Golden Visa

UAE Golden Visa is a long-term, self-sponsored residency route. Qualifying foreign investors, high-earning professionals, and exceptional talent are all eligible. Golden Visa allows you to legally live, work, study, and invest in the United Arab Emirates. You don’t need a traditional sponsor or local employer.

The program was originally introduced to attract foreign talent and investment. But now, it’s a popular residency program.

UAE Golden Visa Requirements

Key eligibility requirements generally include:

Personal requirements

  • Complying fully with the program’s application requirements
  • Getting funds from a legal and verifiable source
  • Providing accurate information

Documents you’ll need

  • Valid original passport (minimum 6 months validity)
  • Passport-size photographs
  • Existing UAE residence visa or entry permit, if applying from inside the country
  • Attested marriage certificate (If applicable)
  • Valid birth certificates for dependent children
  • UAE health insurance coverage

Applicants are also responsible for category-specific documents.

Real estate investors must provide the official Title Deed, developer contract, and bank NOC if the property is mortgaged.

Salaried applicants must provide an attested university degree, a wage certificate, an employment contract, and six months’ worth of bank statements.

Deposit investors must provide a formal bank document verifying the frozen AED 2,000,000 investment.

Talent candidates need to submit a formal letter of reference or nomination from the government. 

Documents not in English must include an authenticated Arabic translation.

Investment requirements

Option 1: Real Estate Investment

  • Minimum AED 2,000,000 (~$545,000 USD) registered on the official Title Deed
  • Applicable administration fees also apply
  • Mortgaged and off-plan properties from approved developers are eligible under specific conditions

Option 2: Public Investment or Fixed Bank Deposit

  • Fixed deposit of AED 2,000,000 in an accredited UAE bank for a minimum of two years, or
  • Company ownership with a minimum annual government tax contribution of AED 250,000

Option 3: Senior Executive Employment

  • Documented basic monthly salary of at least AED 30,000
  • Active UAE employment contract at MOHRE Occupational Level 1 or 2
  • Attested bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited university

Option 4: Exceptional Talent

  • Official government nomination or recommendation from the relevant UAE authority

Option 5: Outstanding Graduates

  • GPA distinction from an accredited UAE university or top-100 global university
  • Average grade of 95% or higher from a UAE high school

Option 6: Entrepreneurs and Startups

  • A project of a technical or future nature with a minimum value of AED 500,000
  • Official approval from an accredited UAE business incubator or relevant authority

How to Get the UAE Golden Visa

The application process has four major stages:

  • Document preparation
  • Eligibility pre-approval
  • Medical screening and biometrics
  • Visa activation

You can start the process from anywhere or while on a visitation visa in the United Arab Emirates. Government offices, legal counsel, or authorised immigration agencies process your application. 

Step 1: Choose your route to UAE Residency

The UAE Golden Visa offers six approved routes.

  • Real Estate Investment

For a property listed on the official Title Deed, the minimum investment is AED 2,000,000 (~$545,000 USD). Off-plan and mortgaged properties are eligible if you get a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the bank. The total valuation registered with the Dubai Land Department (DLD) or local government must be at least AED 2,000,000. The previous requirement for a minimum AED 1 million down payment has been removed. You can combine multiple properties to meet the threshold.

  • Public Investment or Fixed Bank Deposit

A fixed deposit of at least AED 2,000,000 can be made with a UAE bank with accreditation for a minimum of two years. As an alternative, you can own a business or stock in a business that pays a minimum of AED 250,000 in taxes each year. 

  • Senior Executives and Skilled Professionals

This route requires a documented minimum basic monthly salary of AED 30,000. Allowances for housing, transportation, or bonuses do not count toward this threshold. Employment must be at the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) Occupational Level 1 or 2. You must also have a bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited university and an active UAE employment contract.

  • Exceptional Talent and Creative Professionals

This route is for people who are exceptional in their respective fields. Doctors and scientists need approval from the UAE Health Authority or Emirates Scientists Council. Inventors and tech innovators require patents approved by the Ministry of Economy. Creative professionals require an endorsement from the Ministry of Culture and Youth.

  • Outstanding Students and Graduates

Based on academic excellence and GPA, high-achieving graduates from top-100 international colleges or authorised UAE universities may be eligible. With a recommendation from the Ministry of Education, exceptional high school students who receive a final average grade of 95% or higher from a UAE school may also be eligible. 

  • Entrepreneurs and Startups

Founders of innovative or tech-based projects can qualify. They need an auditor’s letter confirming the startup’s minimum value of AED 500,000. A recognized UAE business incubator (AREA 2071 or HUB71) or the Emirate’s authorities must approve the project.

Step 2: Prepare documents

Gather all personal credentials. You must have academic, birth, and marriage certificates translated into Arabic and attested by MOFA (Ministry of Foreign Affairs). You might get assistance from your immigration agent during this procedure.

Step 3: Submit for pre-approval

Use the official portal to submit your nomination. The Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP) in Abu Dhabi and the Northern Emirates handles applications. Dubai applications are processed by the Dubai Land Department or the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA). The pre-approval usually takes 2 to 7 business days. 

Step 4: Complete medical screening and biometrics

After receiving pre-approval, visit an official government medical facility in the UAE. This typically includes a blood test and chest X-ray. They also take a photo and fingerprints for your Emirates ID card. 

Step 5: Receive visa activation and Emirates ID

After medical clearance, your 10-year Golden Visa is activated electronically. Your physical Emirates ID card is issued and delivered shortly after.

What Does the UAE Golden Visa Cost?

Total costs vary depending on the issuing emirate (e.g., Dubai vs. Abu Dhabi). This also depends on whether the applicant applies from inside or outside.

Estimated Fees

  • Real Estate Investors (10-Year): AED 9,885 – 10,140 (approx. $2,690 – $2,760)
  • Salaried Professionals & Executives: AED 4,695 – 5,500 (approx. $1,280 – $1,500) for the primary applicant
  • Family Dependents: AED 5,775 (approx. $1,570) per person

Additional Costs

There are several other mandatory fees:

  • Health Insurance: UAE medical insurance is mandatory for all visa holders.
  • Document Preparation: Costs for legal translation, degree equivalency, and the attestation of foreign documents.
  • Third-Party Services: Agency retainers, typing centre fees, or VIP processing upgrades.

Administrative costs may change over time and are subject to government policies. You should check the latest fee schedules directly with the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship by Investment, Customs & Port Security (ICP).

How Long Does the UAE Golden Visa Last?

The UAE Golden Visa typically lasts for 10 years. As long as you continue to meet the requirements, this is fully renewable.

Validity breakdown by category:

  • Real estate investors: 10 years, renewable if you retain a qualifying property worth AED 2,000,000 or more
  • Public investment or bank deposit: 10 years, renewable if you maintain the required deposit or investment
  • Senior executives and skilled professionals: 10 years, renewable by maintaining qualifying salary and active employment
  • Exceptional talent and outstanding graduates: 10 years, renewable subject to your professional standing or official endorsement
  • Entrepreneurs and business founders: 10 years, renewable subject to maintaining accredited business status or qualifying revenue thresholds

UAE Golden Visa Benefits

UAE Golden Visa holders receive several established benefits.

No physical presence requirement. Standard UAE residence visas become invalid if you remain outside the UAE for more than 180 consecutive days. The Golden Visa waives this rule. You can travel or operate businesses globally.

Family sponsorship

Golden Visa holders can sponsor immediate family members without restrictive caps. This includes your spouse, unmarried sons and daughters of any age, and parents under simplified terms. You can also sponsor unlimited domestic staff. If the primary visa holder passes away, sponsored family members can legally reside in the UAE until their visa permits expire.

Tax benefits

The UAE has no personal income tax on international earnings. The UAE has no capital gains or inheritance tax. Standard corporate tax exemptions apply to qualifying free zone entities and activities. Tax treatment depends on individual applications.

Lifestyle perks

In Dubai, Golden Visa holders get more privileges. This includes the Esaad Privilege Card. You get discounts on healthcare, hospitality, luxury retail, automotive, and real estate services across the UAE.

Limitations

The UAE Golden Visa has some limitations, depending on your route. The real estate route is subject to the official Title Deed value. You can’t use third-party market listings or valuations. This can become a challenge when the policies change.

The UAE banks also verify the source of your funds multiple times.

The Golden Visa does not bypass KYC regulations. For salaried applicants, employment status and minimum salary limits must remain valid at renewal. Real estate investors need to maintain property assets worth AED 2,000,000.

Is the UAE Golden Visa a Good Option?

Yes. For qualifying investors, professionals, and families, the UAE Golden Visa is a good option. You have a 10-year residency in a major, tax-efficient financial hub. You can include eligible family members in the same application. You don’t need to be physically present in the UAE before applying.
